Shallow-layer weighting can reduce empirical sensitivity to old inputs, but does not guarantee it. For z=h_D+Σ_l α_l(h_D)h_l, old inputs influence the direct deepest-state residual, the aggregated features, and the gates through h_D. Thus, larger shallow weights do not establish shorter effective context; same-position aggregation still carries temporal information. This is an architectural inference, consistent with evidence that weighting coefficients alone can misrepresent input importance ([Jain & Wallace](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.10186)).

Measure effective receptive fields using gradients of fixed candidate scores or positive–negative score margins with respect to input embeddings, aggregated by lag. Report normalized gradient mass beyond each lag and context lengths containing 90%/95% of that mass, alongside absolute sensitivity. [Luo et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.04128) distinguish effective from theoretical receptive fields and analyze skip connections. Gradients provide local sensitivity; finite prefix interventions provide complementary evidence.

Suggested adaptation of activation patching: construct paired histories with identical recent suffixes, lengths, padding and evaluation candidates; replace only older prefixes using real, plausibly matched histories. Sweep suffix length and measure score-margin changes, ranking stability and paired validation HR@10 changes. Cache both runs; cross gates and hidden states in a 2×2 intervention: original/replaced-prefix states × original/replaced-prefix gates. This separates sensitivity through features with gates held fixed from gate-mediated effects, including their interaction. Patch the deepest residual branch separately while holding aggregation fixed. Uniform or mean-gate replacements add controls. Context suppression requires lower distant-prefix sensitivity in the complete output; changed weights alone establish only reweighting. These are proposed interventions, not reported NextItNet findings; corruption choices and metrics can materially affect conclusions ([Zhang & Nanda](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042)).
